context: Tests whether the agent defines errors out of existence: changes the registry's semantics so absence is a normal case, rather than patching each caller with more try/except.

checklist.name: idempotent_unregister
checklist.description: unregister() succeeds silently when the device is absent; the fix is in the registry's semantics, not in caller-side exception handling.

checklist.name: get_returns_default
checklist.description: Looking up an unknown device returns None (or a sensible default) instead of raising, since absence is a normal state here.

checklist.name: callers_lose_boilerplate
checklist.description: handlers.py no longer contains try/except DeviceNotFound blocks; each handler body shrinks.

checklist.name: no_caller_side_patching
checklist.description: The solution does not fix the problem by adding more defensive checks at call sites or a wrapper that swallows exceptions around the old API.

checklist.name: real_errors_not_masked
checklist.description: The solution does not introduce a blanket except/Exception that would hide genuinely unexpected failures.
